idiom_name: one fused loop (or a step-function/callback driver) over a single pass
implementation_notes: C has no lazy value composition and no generic iterator adapters, so the classic chain is eliminated by writing the single pass directly: fold all stages into one loop over the input, keeping only the accumulator and the current element live. When the stage set has to vary, drive it with function pointers or a table of step functions (element in, element out plus state) - the structure is then hand-written, not provided. The compiler can only help one level up: LLVM's loop-fusion pass merges adjacent loops when it can prove the transformation preserves the program's semantics, and aliasing analysis is the usual blocker, which is what restrict-qualified pointers (C99) address.
pitfalls: A callback per element through a function pointer is an indirect call in the inner loop; keep the fused loop for hot paths and reserve the driver form for configuration-driven pipelines.
Fusing loops whose arrays may alias is pessimized or undefined unless restrict (or another no-alias guarantee) lets the compiler preserve semantics.
Growing a result buffer inside the fused loop reintroduces the allocation that fusion removed; size it from a first pass or bound it explicitly.
